note: Four Western authorities uniformly date the Diamond Sutra to 868 CE (11 May 868 per Wang Jie's colophon); no disagreement on the year. NOTE: all routes Anglophone/Western; encyclopedias not de-duplicated.
All agree traditional inventor = Cai Lun (Wade-Giles 'Ts'ai Lun' = same person); caveat: paper fragments predate 105 CE but that doesn't contest the traditional credit. Western routes only.
All agree Bi Sheng (Northern Song, d.1051); only romanization varies (Pi Sheng = Bi Sheng). Western routes only; britannica/ebsco/worldhistory recur across items.

Authorities do NOT factually disagree: printing originates in China (woodblock ~7th c.; Bi Sheng movable type 1041-48), Gutenberg credited only with the European mechanical metal-type press (~1440s). 'China vs Gutenberg' is contested purely BY DEFINITION (technique vs the press), not by genuine disagreement -> a legitimate definitional fan.

Unanimous: gun invented in China (gunpowder 9th c., fire lance 10th-12th c., hand cannons 13th c.); Europe adopts firearms 1320s. The 'contested' framing is a definitional nuance WITHIN the Chinese timeline (fire-lance vs true gun), not a China-vs-Europe disagreement -> genuinely settled on origin.

ORIGIN is settled-Chinese, but the FRAMING is live: the 'Four Great Inventions' grouping was coined in the West (Bacon/Needham) and scholars (Deng Yinke; Tandfonline 'Tradition of Invention') critique it as a constructed/nationalist frame because the mature world-shaping forms diffused cross-culturally -> 'shared heritage' is a defensible scholarly reading. The harvest SPLITS (4 chinese / 1 shared).
